summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with relapsed multiple myeloma, autoimmune hemolytic anemia, type 2 diabetes, and diastolic heart failure, was admitted for fever and weakness. Evaluation revealed pneumonia and bilateral lower extremity cellulitis. He was treated with IV antibiotics, later transitioned to oral levofloxacin, and received IVIG for low antibody levels. His diabetes required insulin regimen adjustment due to fluctuations. Hypertension was managed with addition of losartan. Renal function remained stable despite baseline CKD, and proteinuria was monitored without biopsy due to bleeding risk. Anemia improved with supportive care. He recovered well, with resolution of fever and respiratory symptoms, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics and optimized medical management with follow-up arranged.
